specGaps: SG-A — THE BINARY CANNOT BE RUN AT HEAD (the one real hole in plan:2856). src/main.cpp:9-14 is the 11.1 scaffold: no argc/argv, no config load, no Router. No earlier task's bullet claims the CLI, and 11.8 is the first task that runs the binary at all. RESOLUTION: 11.8 lands the minimum CLI, TDD'd — NEW header-only src/router/cli.hpp exporting a PURE parse (`struct CliOptions { std::string configPath; std::string schemaPath; bool showHelp{false}; bool showVersion{false}; };`, `struct CliParse { std::optional<CliOptions> options; std::string error; std::string usage; };`, `[[nodiscard]] CliParse parseCli(std::span<const std::string_view> args)` where `args` EXCLUDES argv[0]) + NEW src/tests/cli_test.cpp (row 11.8-cli-contract, real doctest, RED first as a compile failure) + src/main.cpp wiring that is a thin adapter over it: parseCli → read the config file → parseRouterConfig(text, schemaPath) → applyLoggingLevel → Router router{cfg} → start() → park until SIGINT/SIGTERM → stop(). Rationale for putting it HERE rather than folding it into 11.7: 11.7 is a metrics module task whose bullet says nothing about process lifecycle, and the CLI's only consumer before 12.1 is this smoke. Rationale for the pure/thin split: a manual smoke must not be the FIRST proof that argument handling works, and the parse is the only part of a process entry point that is deterministically testable.

SG-B — WHERE DOES THE JSON SCHEMA FILE COME FROM AT RUNTIME? parseRouterConfig (config.hpp:406) takes a schemaPath and reads it on every parse; the only schema in the tree is src/tests/schemas/RouterConfig.schema.json, a build-time export into the SOURCE tree that a deployed binary has no business locating by guesswork. RESOLUTION: `--schema <path>` is a REQUIRED flag with NO default and NO search path. Inventing a search path (exe-relative, cwd-relative, $PREFIX/share) would create a second source of truth for the config shape — exactly what the exported-schema design exists to prevent — and a wrong guess would fail at startup with a file-not-found rather than a named field. The smoke passes the repo path explicitly; 12.1's serve.py passes whatever path it generates against. Recorded so 12.1 inherits a stated contract instead of a discovered one.

SG-C — THE CONFIG FILE IS NOT COMMITTABLE. §2.2's path is .data/configs/conductor-router.json and .data/ is gitignored (.gitignore:2); the file is generated by serve.py at 12.1, which has not happened. RESOLUTION: the smoke hand-writes .data/configs/conductor-router.json (§2.2 explicitly says "generated by serve.py, hand-editable") and the artifact reproduces its FULL text verbatim, because the run is otherwise unreproducible — a live artifact that cites a file no reader can see is not evidence. The file itself is never added to git and 11.8 never edits .gitignore.

RESOLUTION: the condition is FALSE — record `dashboard: NOT BUILT` with the CMake evidence (the absence of the target, cited by file) and make no rendering claim of any kind. 11.8 does NOT add an ftxui target: nothing in the acceptance list depends on the dashboard, and adding a UI target inside a live-smoke task is scope creep that would also drag ftxui into a Phase 11 build that deliberately excludes it (branch-b-plan.md:58 "NO llama, NO ftxui"). Row 11.8-dashboard-not-built pins the honest record.

SG-E — WHICH admission.maxInflightPerModel FOR THE SMOKE? §4.4 (plan:1646-1650) makes it normative that maxInflightPerModel MUST be ≤ llama-server's `--parallel` slot count, and serve.py at HEAD passes no `--parallel` at all (serve.py:236-248), so the true slot count is unmeasured until 12.1. RESOLUTION: use the §2.2 document VERBATIM, maxInflightPerModel 4 included, and drive the smoke's requests ONE AT A TIME so the cap is never approached and the unverified ≤ obligation is never exercised. Diverging from §2.2 would mean the live run and the 11.2 config doctests describe different documents for no gain. The artifact records, in words, that the ≤ obligation remains UNVERIFIED and is 12.1's — folded into row 11.8-binding-not-discharged.

SG-F — DOES 11.8 DISCHARGE 11.1 STEP 2? It runs live against llama-server, so the temptation is real. RESOLUTION: NO. 11.8 legitimately observes four of Step 2's six items (the /v1/models shape as seen THROUGH the router, response_format/json_schema acceptance + GBNF constraining, usage+timings in a non-stream response, SSE framing) and records them under its OWN heading. It cannot produce item 6, the effective concurrent slot count for N∈{1,2,4,8} with and without --parallel, which is the load-bearing number, nor item 5's autoload latency in the serve.py-generated configuration. The `WIRE_CONTRACT_VERIFIED:` stamp therefore stays `<pending>` and the `## Binding` paragraph stays intact. Row 11.8-binding-not-discharged.

SG-G — WHEN IS THE METRICS LINE OBSERVABLE? The smoke wants to `tail` the ledger while the router is still up, which only works if 11.7 appends-and-flushes per request rather than buffering to shutdown. RESOLUTION: 11.8 asserts the line is present AFTER the response completes and BEFORE the router is stopped (row 11.8-metrics-line). This is a constraint 11.7 must satisfy; it is the only behaviour that lets a running router be diagnosed at all, and a buffered ledger would also lose every line when the 12.1 supervisor restarts the process after a crash — the exact situation the ledger exists to explain. Raised at the Phase 11 gate so 11.7's own spec pins it explicitly rather than inheriting it from here.

SG-H — ATTEMPT-ONCE, AND NOT DISTURBING A RUNNING SERVER. branch-b-plan.md:85-89 makes the live probe attempt-once with BLOCKED+commands as an acceptable outcome, and the repo habitually keeps a llama-server on 8080 that the user may be using. RESOLUTION: (1) if 127.0.0.1:8080 is ALREADY serving (GET /health 200), REUSE it and record that fact plus the pid/argv actually observed — never start a competing server and never kill one; (2) the router binds 8088 per §2.2, so it cannot collide with the upstream; (3) if the smoke cannot run (model absent, OOM, port unavailable, upstream refuses the schema'd request), the artifact records BLOCKED plus every command attempted and its raw failure output, and the task still commits — a recorded BLOCKED is a true statement about the system, an invented transcript is not.

SG-I — EXIT CODES AND SIGNAL HANDLING (unstated anywhere; a manual operator needs them and the 12.1 supervisor will branch on them). RESOLUTION, pinned here so 12.1 inherits them: 0 = clean shutdown after SIGINT or SIGTERM (Router::stop() ran); 2 = usage error, message on stderr naming the offending or missing flag, followed by the usage text; 3 = ConfigError, stderr contains ConfigError::field() verbatim (empty field ⇒ the schema-file message, which names the path); 4 = listen bind failure, stderr contains host:port. Only the exit-2 family is doctest-reachable (it is a pure parse verdict); the others are recorded live from raw output.

assertions.text: DOCTEST (src/tests/cli_test.cpp, RED first as a compile failure — src/router/cli.hpp does not exist): parseCli is a PURE function of its argument span (which excludes argv[0]) and pins, case by case: `--config P --schema Q` yields engaged options with configPath==P and schemaPath==Q and an empty error, in either flag order; a MISSING --config, and a missing --schema, each yield disengaged options and an error naming that exact flag string; a flag given with no following value yields an error naming that flag rather than consuming the next flag as its value; an UNKNOWN flag and a bare positional argument each yield an error quoting the offending token verbatim; a REPEATED --config (or --schema) is an error naming it, never last-wins; `--help` and `--version` are accepted ALONE (no --config required) and set exactly their own bool with an empty error; the usage text is non-empty and names both required flags. No filesystem access, no getenv, no globals — the same argument vector yields the same CliParse every call
